7 04-04-2025 1.
Heard learned Counsel for the appellant and learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State.

2. The present appeal has been preferred by the appellant against the judgment of conviction dated 23.11.2022 and order of sentence dated 30.11.2022, passed by learned Principal Judge, Special Court-M.P./M.L.A., Aurangabad, Bihar in Sessions Trial No. 247 of 2020 (arising out of Haspura Police Station Case No. 36 of 2018), whereby the appellant has been convicted for the charge under Sections 302/498A of the Indian Penal Code and Section 27 of Arms Act.

sentences.text: By the impugned judgment and order of sentence, the appellant has been sentenced to undergo imprisonment for life with a fine of Rs. 20,000/- under Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code and in default of payment of fine, the appellant has further to undergo additional imprisonment for 04 months.

The appellant has further been sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for 03 years with a fine of Rs. 5,000/- under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code and in default of payment of fine, the appellant has further to undergo additional imprisonment for 02 months.

The appellant has further been sentenced to undergo rigouros imprisonment for 07 years with a fine of Rs.
10,000/- under Section 27 of Arms Act and in default of payment of fine, the appellant has further to undergo additional imprisonment for 03 months.
5. The prosecution story, in brief, is that the marriage of informant's niece was solemnized with the appellant Rahul Kumar @ Rahul Sharma in the year 2010.
It is alleged that after the birth of female child, the informant's son-in-law started torturing the deceased and pressurized her to bring money from her parents.

It has further been alleged that in the year 2015, the appellant shot Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.78 of 2023(7) dt.04-04-2025 dead the daughter of his master (employer),
for which a case was lodged against him and he remained in jail for one year.
It has also been alleged that on the date of occurrence, the appellant shot dead the informant's niece.
The informant also got the information that the appellant has sustained injury in his shoulder and was admitted in the hospital.

6. Learned Counsel for the appellant submits that on the date of occurrence, somebody entered into the house of the appellant, shot dead of his wife and in the firing, the appellant also sustained injury,
for which, he was admitted in the hospital.
Learned counsel further submits that the appellant informed the Police, upon which, Police arrived and inquest report was prepared.
The appellant is stated to be in custody since 14.03.2018.
7. On the other hand, learned APP for the State argued that appellant is the main assailant and under Section 106 of the Evidence Act, the onus is upon the appellant to explain.
Nonetheless, the appellant failed to produce the medical evidence to show that appellant sustained bullet injury on the date of occurrence and was treated by a Doctor.

8. Considering the nature of allegation and the evidence adduced during course of trial, we are not inclined to grant bail to the appellant during the pendency of this appeal, accordingly, the same is rejected.
However the appellant is at liberty to renew his Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.78 of 2023(7) dt.04-04-2025 prayer after completion of one year from today.
9. I.A. No. 1 of 2024 is dismissed.

(Anil Kumar Sinha, J) ( Chandra Prakash Singh, J) rinkee/-
